Metadata.Summary: Derm Foundation is a machine learning model designed to accelerate AI development for skin image analysis in dermatology applications using pre-trained embeddings. It produces a 6144-dimensional embedding vector as output.
Metadata.Keywords: machine learning; dermatology; image analysis; embeddings; skin conditions; AI

UsesAndDirections.IntendedUseAndWorkflow: Derm Foundation reduces the data, compute, and expertise needed to develop task-specific models for skin image analysis. It can classify clinical conditions, score severity, identify body parts, and determine image quality.
UsesAndDirections.PrimaryIntendedUsers: Businesses and institutions in healthcare and life sciences.
UsesAndDirections.HowToUse: Use example code snippets to run the model locally or create a production version using Model Garden. Load images, format input, load the model from Hugging Face Hub, call inference, and extract the embedding vector.

Warnings.ModelLimitations: Derm Foundation's quality can degrade in extreme lighting/noise conditions. It was trained on data from the US, Colombia, Australia and public images and may not generalize well to other countries, patient populations, or image types. It only generates embeddings and does not generate predictions or diagnoses. [SOURCE 1]

TrustIngredients.OutcomesAndOutput: The model produces a 6144-dimensional embedding vector as output, which can be used for downstream tasks like classifying skin conditions and scoring severity [SOURCE 1]
TrustIngredients.TypeAndValueOfSolutionOutput: Embedding vector of floating point values (Dimensions: 6144) [SOURCE 1]
TrustIngredients.ExplanationForHowAnOutputIsGenerated: Derm Foundation is pre-trained on large amounts of labeled skin images to produce 6144 dimensional embeddings that capture dense features relevant for analyzing these images. [SOURCE 1]
TrustIngredients.InputDataSource: A large number of health-related image-text pairs from the public web and tele-dermatology datasets from the United States and Colombia, a skin cancer dataset from Australia, and additional public images. [SOURCE 1]
TrustIngredients.OutputInputDataType: Input: PNG image file 448 x 448 pixels [SOURCE 1]
TrustIngredients.DevelopmentDataCharacterization: Derm Foundation was trained in two stages. First, pre-training used contrastive learning on public image-text pairs. Second, the image component was fine-tuned for condition classification and other downstream tasks using clinical datasets from teledermatology services in the United States and Colombia, a skin cancer dataset from Australia, and additional public images. [SOURCE 1]
TrustIngredients.TrainingData: The model was trained in two stages: pre-training on a large number of health-related image-text pairs from the public web and supervised fine-tuning on teledermatology datasets from the United States and Colombia, a skin cancer dataset from Australia, and additional public images. The images come from smartphone cameras, other cameras, and dermatoscopes and may have been taken by clinicians or self-captured by patients. [SOURCE 1]
TrustIngredients.DemographicRepresentativeness: The supervised fine-tuned model was trained using data from a limited set of countries (United States, Colombia, Australia, and public images). It may not generalize well to data from other countries or patient populations not used in training. [SOURCE 1]
TrustIngredients.RelevanceOfTrainingDataToIntendedPopulat: The model may not generalize well to data from other countries, patient populations, or image types not used in training.

UsefulnessEfficacy.GoalOfMetrics: Derm Foundation was evaluated for data-efficient accuracy across skin-related classification tasks. [SOURCE 1]
UsefulnessEfficacy.Result: Training a linear classifier on Derm-Foundation embeddings were substantially more performant (10-15% increase in accuracy) than doing the same for a standard BiT-M model across different proportions of training data. [SOURCE 1]
UsefulnessEfficacy.Interpretation: Models built on top of Derm Foundation embeddings for dermatology-related tasks achieved significantly higher quality than those built solely on embeddings or fine-tuned from BiT-M; this advantage was most pronounced for smaller training dataset sizes. [SOURCE 4]
UsefulnessEfficacy.TestType: Evaluated for data-efficient accuracy across a range of skin-related classifications tasks using a linear classifier on Derm-Foundation embeddings. [SOURCE 1, SOURCE 4]
UsefulnessEfficacy.TestingDataDescription: A linear classifier was trained on Derm-Foundations embeddings and compared to a standard BiT-M model across different proportions of training data. [SOURCE 1]
